requirement:
{impl}`requirements.configuration.feature_sections`
Configuration names MUST match `[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]*` and be case-sensitive.
Project-selection keys MUST be canonical absolute project-root paths. Model IDs
MUST be nonempty opaque strings, preserving tags and ARNs. `api_key_env` MUST
name a nonempty environment variable without `=` or NUL.

Authoring MUST validate its fields under {cite}`requirements.configuration.loading`.
The `options` map MUST accept backend-defined inference settings rather than a
closed Habeas list; the adapter MUST pass them through Rig's provider parameter
mechanism and report rejection by Rig or the provider. These options MUST NOT
replace the selected model, the assessment prompt, or tool definitions.
rationale:
## Obligation review

The source and referenced tests satisfy `requirements.authoring.configuration_storage`.

| Obligation | Implementation and verification |
|---|---|
| Configuration names match `[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]*`. | `src/config.rs#fn[validate_name]` checks the first byte and every subsequent byte. It is reached through `UserConfig::parse` → validation and through resolution. `tests/configuration.rs#fn[storage_rules_reject_each_invalid_field_with_its_setting]` covers empty names, invalid initial characters, punctuation, whitespace, non-ASCII names, and accepted mixed-case/hyphen/underscore names. |
| Names are case-sensitive. | `src/config.rs#struct[UserAuthoringConfig]` stores names as distinct `String` keys; resolution uses exact map lookup in `src/config.rs#fn[resolve_authoring_with_workspace_from]`. The storage-rules test preserves both `Local` and `local`; `tests/configuration.rs#fn[explicit_project_and_default_selections_choose_whole_configs]` rejects `DEFAULT` when only `default` exists. |
| Project-selection keys are canonical and absolute project-root paths. | `src/config.rs#impl[UserAuthoringConfig]/fn[validate]` rejects relative paths, noncanonical component spellings, trailing separators, and existing paths whose canonical spelling differs. The storage-rules test exercises those failures, including a symlink, and accepts canonical existing and not-yet-created roots. `tests/configuration.rs#fn[user_and_workspace_authoring_tables_round_trip_every_map]` verifies preservation of a canonical project key. |
| Model IDs are nonempty opaque strings, preserving tags and ARNs. | `src/config.rs#impl[BackendConfig]/fn[validate]` checks emptiness without parsing identifiers; `src/config.rs#impl[BackendConfig]/fn[model_ref]` retains their strings. The storage-rules test rejects an empty model and asserts exact tagged-ID preservation. `tests/configuration.rs#fn[user_and_workspace_authoring_tables_round_trip_every_map]` asserts exact ARN and tagged Bedrock identifiers, and `tests/configuration.rs#fn[backend_configuration_round_trips_without_materializing_defaults]` verifies tagged Ollama values and configuration round-tripping. |
| `api_key_env` is nonempty, contains no `=`, and contains no NUL. | `src/config.rs#impl[BackendConfig]/fn[validate]` checks each property. The storage-rules test separately exercises all three failures and an accepted name. |
| Authoring validates its fields under `requirements.configuration.loading`. | `src/config.rs#impl[UserConfig]/fn[parse]` decodes and validates; `src/config.rs#fn[resolve_authoring_with_workspace_from]`, reachable from the marked resolver, validates user and workspace settings. `src/config.rs#fn[invalid]` includes the file and setting in diagnostics. The storage-rules test asserts both for invalid user and workspace fields; `tests/configuration.rs#fn[authoring_concurrency_defaults_overrides_and_invalid_values]` also checks typed-field failures. This assesses authoring's application of loading, not the independent loading requirement as a whole. |
| The options map accepts backend-defined inference settings rather than a closed list. | `src/config.rs#enum[OptionValue]` permits scalar, array, and nested-map values; `src/config.rs#impl[BackendConfig]/fn[options_json]` serializes the map rather than filtering it to recognized inference keys. The round-trip test verifies arbitrary nested provider options. The Ollama, Bedrock, and OpenAI CLI tests referenced by the subject assert transmitted backend options. |
| The adapter passes options through Rig's provider parameter mechanism. | `src/authoring/providers.rs#impl[RigProvider/CompletionProvider]/fn[complete]` assigns remaining options to `additional_params`; its reachable `apply_bedrock_options` maps Converse-native inference fields to Rig request fields. `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[ollama_cli_delivers_sources_records_fixme_and_keeps_usage_content_free]`, `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[bedrock_cli_uses_selected_profile_region_and_converse_tools]`, and `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[openai_responses_replays_tool_calls_and_records_usage]` assert the resulting provider requests on all three backend paths. |
| Rig rejection and provider rejection are reported. | `complete` propagates native-option validation errors and wraps model-call failures through `provider_failure`. `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[provider_rejection_of_inference_options_is_reported]` checks both local Bedrock rejection and an HTTP provider rejection, including their diagnostic content. `src/authoring/providers.rs#mod[tests]/fn[bedrock_native_option_types_are_checked_and_only_max_tokens_is_defaulted]` additionally exercises invalid native option types. |
| Options do not replace the selected model, assessment prompt, or tool definitions. | `src/config.rs#impl[BackendConfig]/fn[validate]` rejects model-, prompt-, conversation-, and tool-replacement keys. The storage-rules test exercises model, prompt, and tool aliases; `tests/configuration.rs#fn[openai_configuration_preserves_model_and_resolves_credentials]` covers OpenAI `input` and `instructions`. The referenced CLI tests also assert selected models and retained prompt/tool content while inference options are present. |

All implementation above is reachable from the subject's marked roots. The tests cited carry subject test references. OpenAI request defaults are specified by the additionally marked `requirements.authoring.openai_defaults`, and the Bedrock token default is specified by `requirements.authoring.output_limit`; neither is an undocumented inference-setting restriction. No unacknowledged gap was found.

text: :::{req} configuration_storage
{impl}`requirements.configuration.feature_sections`
Configuration names MUST match `[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]*` and be case-sensitive.
Project-selection keys MUST be canonical absolute project-root paths. Model IDs
MUST be nonempty opaque strings, preserving tags and ARNs. `api_key_env` MUST
name a nonempty environment variable without `=` or NUL.
Authoring MUST validate its fields under {cite}`requirements.configuration.loading`.
The `options` map MUST accept backend-defined inference settings rather than a
closed Habeas list; the adapter MUST pass them through Rig's provider parameter
mechanism and report rejection by Rig or the provider. These options MUST NOT
replace the selected model, the assessment prompt, or tool definitions.
:::{req} loading
An operation MUST load user configuration only when its requirements call for
user settings. A missing user file MUST represent absent user configuration;
whether the operation can proceed MUST be defined by the feature. Loading MUST
NOT create a file, repair malformed input, or supply an undocumented selection.
When loading configuration, Habeas MUST report unreadable files, invalid TOML,
unsupported user-file versions, unknown common keys, and invalid common field
types. It MUST validate the feature sections used by that operation and report
invalid feature settings with the file and setting identified. Unknown keys in
an explicitly documented provider-owned options map MUST follow that feature's
validation rules.
An operation MUST NOT require or semantically validate configuration for a
feature it does not use. This isolation MUST NOT suppress TOML syntax errors in
a shared file that the operation otherwise needs to parse. In particular,
ordinary validation still requires a parseable `book.toml` while remaining
independent of authoring settings and the user configuration file. It MUST apply
the selected workspace's evidence path policy without loading its model clients
or credentials.
:::{req} openai_defaults
{impl}`requirements.configuration.feature_sections`
An OpenAI configuration MAY omit `model`; the effective model MUST then be
`gpt-6.1-sol`. When `options.reasoning.effort` is omitted, the request MUST use
`low` effort, preserving other reasoning options. When `options.max_output_tokens`
is omitted, the request MUST use an output-token limit of 16,384. These option
defaults MUST apply even when the model is overridden. An explicit model,
reasoning effort, or output-token limit MUST override its corresponding default.
Defaults MUST NOT be written into omitted configuration fields on serialization.
An explicitly empty model MUST still be rejected.
:::{req} feature_sections
Each configurable feature MUST define the name and typed data structure of its
user section and any supported project section, citing these common configuration
requirements. The feature MUST specify its supported keys, value types, defaults,
validation rules, and the precedence or combination rules for user settings,
project settings, and invocation options. It MUST specify the behavior of an
absent section and which operations require that section.
Feature-specific fields MUST stay within the feature's section. A feature MUST
NOT reinterpret another feature's settings or change the shared file locations
or schema version. A feature MAY define a provider-owned options map, but MUST
document that boundary and how those options are validated.
:::{req} serialization
Saved configuration MUST remain distinct from resolved runtime configuration.
Serializing and deserializing a valid configuration MUST preserve its semantic
values, including explicit versus omitted settings. Optional fields MAY be
omitted on serialization; defaults and environment-derived values MUST NOT be
materialized into omitted fields. TOML comments and formatting need not
round-trip.
Loading configuration or running a configured feature MUST NOT rewrite the user
or project configuration as a side effect. Resolved credentials and live runtime
objects MUST NOT enter the serialized data structures. Explicitly supplied
credential values are permitted only in the fields documented by the authoring
feature; credentials resolved from a profile or environment MUST NOT be written
back to configuration.
:::{req} output_limit
When a Bedrock configuration sets no `maxTokens` option, each provider request
MUST ask for at most 16,384 output tokens. A configured `maxTokens` MUST be used
as given.
When a response stops because it reached a known output limit, the harness MUST
continue the same conversation once, adding a user message with an error result
for each tool call in the cut-off response, followed by this text with `<limit>`
replaced by the limit:
```text
Your previous response reached the <limit>-token output limit and was cut off,
so its tool call was incomplete. Keep within the limit: make your rationale
shorter, then call the tool again.
A second response that reaches the limit, or a response that stops at an
output limit that is not known, MUST fail the assessment as an incomplete
response. Where the provider reports whether a response stopped at the output
limit or because the conversation exceeded the model's context window, the
harness SHOULD continue only the former and fail the assessment on the latter;
where it does not, the stop MUST be treated as reaching the output limit.
